column1: # Boundary guard — TIER 1: shape patterns, safe to publish (DOR-2024).
# WIRE FORMAT, shared with the private tier-2 ruleset delivered through the
# BOUNDARY_TERMS Actions secret, so ONE loader reads both and the two halves
# cannot drift: one rule per line, <rule-id> TAB <extended regular expression>.
# A leading # is a comment, a blank line is ignored, and there is no third
# column — every extra field is another thing a consumer can mis-split.
# Patterns are matched case-insensitively, one input line at a time, and stay
# inside the POSIX-ERE subset that JavaScript's RegExp also accepts (no
# lookaround, no \\b), so the private half can be authored once and consumed by
# either. Case-insensitivity is why boundaries here are spelled [^A-Za-z]
# rather than [a-z] tricks: under /i a case-based distinction does not exist.
# RULE IDS ARE STABLE AND ARE NEVER REUSED OR RENUMBERED. A guard reports the
# id and only the id, so an id that changes meaning silently changes what every
# past failure meant. Blocks are allocated by category, with gaps inside each:
#   BND-1xx  local filesystem paths              — tier 2, see below
#   BND-2xx  private-looking hostnames           — tier 1, here
#   BND-3xx  money-shaped strings near plan words — tier 1, here
#   BND-4xx  workspace and repository identifiers — tier 2
#   BND-9xx  exact private terms                  — tier 2
# WHY BLOCK 1xx IS NOT HERE, THOUGH A LOCAL ABSOLUTE PATH IS THE MOST OBVIOUS
# SHAPE IN THE WHOLE GUARD. Measured against this tree on 2026-09-15: a plain
# /Users/<name>/... pattern matches 238 lines and /home/<name>/... another 98,
# and essentially all of them are legitimate — this is software that resolves,
# renders and tests other people's home directories, so example paths are
# everyday vocabulary in fixtures, showcases, docs and specs. The thing that
# separates a leak from a fixture is not the SHAPE of the path; it is whose
# name is in it. A username and a personal folder name are VALUES, and a
# committed pattern for a value publishes the value. Block 1xx therefore lives
# in the private ruleset, alongside 4xx and 9xx, for exactly the reason a
# repository name does.
# Every id below needs a one-line public description in SHAPE_RULE_NOTES in
# scripts/check-boundary.ts; scripts/__tests__/check-boundary.test.ts fails if
# the two lists disagree.
# A host whose leftmost label names an internal-facing service, under a real
# registrable domain. The public app talks to one documented origin; a host
# like this in public source is either a control-plane endpoint or a copy of
# somebody's internal infrastructure.
BND-201
# --- BND-3xx: money-shaped strings near plan-shaped words -----------------
# AGENTS.md: "Never add prices, plan names, margins or supplier terms to this
# repo; the pricing page announces them first." Two rules because the two
# orders read differently and a single pattern for both is unreadable.
BND-301
BND-302
# A margin, the third category AGENTS.md names, stated as a percentage. The
# financial qualifier is REQUIRED: a bare "margin" is a CSS property, and a
# rule that fires on layout prose is a rule everyone learns to skip.
BND-303
